note: Returns are after slippage and delivery charges. Excess is against every universe stock bought the same morning for the same hold. The t-statistic is on each entry day's average; holds overlap, so it overstates certainty for the longer holds.

results.label: Jump on results
results.basis: Up 5% or more over the two sessions around results, on 1.5 times the usual turnover.

results.label: Big jump on results
results.basis: Up 8% or more around results, on 3 times the usual turnover.

results.label: Fall on results
results.basis: Down 5% or more over the two sessions around results. Expected to keep lagging.

results.label: New 52-week high
results.basis: First close above the highest close of the last year.

results.label: New 52-week high on volume
results.basis: The same, on twice the usual turnover.

results.label: Breakout from a tight three-month range
results.basis: Close above the highest close of the last 63 sessions, when those sessions stayed within a 25% range, on 1.5 times the usual turnover.

results.label: Strong stock back above its 20-day average
results.basis: Up 50% or more over 12 months, above the 50-day average, closing back above the 20-day average after a close below it.

results.label: Enters the top 5% on 12-month momentum
results.basis: The stock's 12-month return (skipping the last month) moves into the top 5% of the universe.

results.label: Heavy delivery buying over a week
results.basis: Delivery share over five sessions 1.5 times its 20-day average, with the price up over the week.

results.label: Bounce from a three-month low
results.basis: Closed at a 63-session low within the last five sessions and is now up 5% from it, above the 200-day average.

bookNote: Each rule run as a book of Rs 5 lakh: limited positions, whole shares, delivery charges, 0.1% slippage a side, capital gains tax paid each March. Idle cash earns nothing. NIFTY 500 is the price index, without dividends, costs or tax.
overlapNote: Monthly returns of the results book against the Monthly Plan's Growth mode, both after tax. Drawdowns here are on month-end values, so they are shallower than the daily figures above.
